Good afternoon, judges. We are Team Avengers. Every day, a kirana owner generates data: bills, payments, customers, stock. But turning that data into decisions takes time and experience they do not have. For Track 1 we built Disha, an AI business partner that tells a merchant what to do today and helps them do it. Let me start with the problem.

name: Text 64
text: The problem isn't a lack of data. It's the lack of a partner who turns data into action.

Paytm made accepting payments easy. Running the business is still guesswork, and five things go wrong quietly. A bill is keyed at 69 rupees instead of 96. A regular customer disappears for a month. The shelf empties right before a festival. Cash planning happens from memory. And dashboards are in English, when the merchant thinks in Telugu. The problem is not a lack of data. It is the lack of a partner who turns data into action. So here is what we built.

name: Text 46
text: Disha doesn't wait for the right question. It surfaces what matters.

Disha runs one loop every morning: observe, detect, prioritise, explain, act and learn. The merchant does not open twenty charts. At 8 AM they see three priorities, in plain language. Disha prepares the action, and the merchant approves it. Let me show you what that looks like on three scenarios.

name: Text 56
text: All figures are illustrative synthetic sandbox data · Conceptual prototype interfaces · Nothing is sent or ordered without merchant approval

Scenario one. Bill 1048, sugar 2 kg: expected price 96, recorded 69, a gap of 27 rupees. The digits look swapped. Disha flags it for review rather than silently fixing it, because it could be a legitimate discount. Scenario two. Lakshmi usually visits every 14 days and has now been away 30. Disha shows why she is flagged, drafts a Telugu message, and waits for the merchant's approval. Scenario three. Ghee: 5 units on hand, 18 sold a week, so about 2.57 a day. That is 1.9 days of stock. Reorder 24: a week of demand plus a buffer of 6. The ghee forecast is based on recent sales velocity; festival demand uplift is not yet modelled. Every number here is computed by code, and all data is synthetic sandbox data. [Switch to the live prototype demo here.]

name: Text 53
text: Every recommendation has a reason. Every consequential action has approval. Every action has an audit trail.

Under the hood Disha is an agent, not a chat window. A signal arrives, the agent picks a tool, deterministic code calculates, it recommends, the merchant approves, and only then does it execute and log. Our design has seven tools, shown here; the cash-flow tool is planned for phase two. The merchant can also just speak: here they ask in Telugu how much ghee is left, and Disha answers from validated inventory numbers. In our sandbox, messaging is simulated. Next: why you can trust those numbers.

name: Text 50
text: Prototype runs on synthetic Paytm-like sandbox data. No live Paytm API integration is claimed; production integration is a future step needing Paytm access and approval.

Four layers. The merchant app. An agent orchestrator that routes tools and manages approvals. A deterministic engine for reconciliation, customer intelligence, inventory and cash flow. And a data and AI layer. The key idea: the deterministic engine calculates the numbers and the LLM only explains them. The LLM never does arithmetic and never decides eligibility. Every number in the narration is validated against the computed facts, and if the check fails we show a template instead. Where a tool says option, the final choice is not fixed yet. Our data is synthetic Paytm-like sandbox data. We do not claim a live Paytm integration; that would be a future step with Paytm's access and approval.

Dashboards show history. Chat assistants answer when asked. Disha comes to the merchant every morning with computed numbers, an action already prepared, and a human approval step before anything consequential happens. That combination, proactive, computed, acting with approval and voice-first, is what we think makes it different. We are comparing categories of tools, not naming any competitor.

Our proposed model has three steps: free basic insights, a premium merchant subscription, and then financial-services opportunities with authorised partners, who make every credit or insurance decision. This is Disha's proposal, not an existing Paytm product or agreement. Separately, here is what Paytm itself reported for Q2 FY27, quarter ended 30 September 2026: 1.64 crore merchants on subscription plans, and 912 crore rupees of revenue from distribution of financial services, up 49 percent year on year. Paytm also reports AI agent-powered merchant sales and service, supporting targeted acquisition, deeper engagement, cross-sell and lower cost-to-serve. Disha is a concrete concept that fits that direction.

Our roadmap has three phases. Phase 1 is the hackathon MVP you have just seen. Phase 2, subject to Paytm's access and approval, is a sandbox pilot, which we propose as around 50 merchants in Hyderabad and Andhra Pradesh. Phase 3 is production scale, only after the pilot validates quality. Our ask is simple: build Disha with Paytm, validate one real merchant problem in a focused pilot, and scale what works. Paytm already connects merchants to digital payments. Disha can help connect those payments to better business decisions. Every merchant deserves a business partner. Thank you, we are Team Avengers, and we are happy to take questions.
